A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Spatial-Mamba. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Spatial-Mamba experiments on ImageNet-1K, COCO and ADE20K, component ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Cascade Mask R-CNN results, SASF integration experiments and a fusion-operator comparison.

M1.justification: The core Spatial-Mamba architecture and equations remain unchanged. Appendix F adds SASF adaptations for Vim and VMamba and a dynamic-convolution fusion variant. The Vim adaptation replaces the middle class token with average pooling and sets the state dimension to 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K classification, COCO detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K semantic segmentation. The added detector head, backbone adaptations and fusion-operator experiment retain this data and task coverage.

E2.justification: Existing benchmark comparator lists are retained. New Table 7 compares SASF-equipped Vim and VMamba against their unaugmented controls, while Table 8 introduces dynamic convolution as an evaluated alternative to depth-wise fusion.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds COCO evaluation with Cascade Mask R-CNN under a 3× schedule for the Tiny and Small backbones. Appendix F adds backbone and fusion-operator configurations. The previously reported training budgets, metrics and main benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F substantially broadens the design analyses by testing SASF in multidirectional backbones and comparing fusion operators' accuracy and throughput. Figure 5 adds spatial activation maps, and new Figure 6 supplies additional before-and-after state-fusion examples. The original ablations, ERF analysis and downstream qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The newly documented 50-image ERF sample describes visualization sampling, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 6–8 add substantive results: Cascade Spatial-Mamba-T/S achieve box/mask AP of 52.1/44.9 and 53.3/45.8; SASF-equipped Vim-Ti and VMamba-T score 72.2% and 82.9%; dynamic fusion scores 83.7% with throughput 907 versus 83.5% and 1438 for depth-wise fusion. Under the retained Table 2 Mask R-CNN 3× setting, Spatial-Mamba-T's mask AP/AP50/AP75 change from 43.6/67.6/46.9 to 43.8/67.8/47.2. Other existing numerical tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The SSM equations and matrix-unification reasoning are retained. Former Appendix B becomes Appendix C, with the original derivation split into Equations 7–8 and rewritten using equivalent product notation. No substantive mathematical assumptions, proofs or results are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims: structure-aware state fusion enables effective single-scan visual modeling, competitive benchmark performance, and a shared matrix formulation with Mamba and linear attention.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds an interpretation of activation maps as capturing distant relevant regions. Appendix F argues that SASF also benefits multidirectional models and discusses flexible fusion operators' computational costs. Appendix G additionally attributes the larger initial ERF to neighborhood connectivity.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies state dimension 1, CUDA changes separating state transition from observation, and GEMM-based SASF implementation. It also documents the existing ERF procedure: gradients on 50 randomly selected ImageNet-1K validation images resized to 1024×1024. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to the earlier experiments; code/model access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Cascade R-CNN, dynamic convolution and deformable convolution, supporting the added experiments and operator discussion. The main related-work section and positioning relative to previous visual SSMs remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds an appendix roadmap, reorganizes the appendices, updates cross-references and makes localized explanatory and language edits. It also adds the ICLR publication header. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The visual evidence is substantially expanded: Figure 5 connects matrices to input-image activation maps, new Figure 6 displays additional state-fusion examples, and Tables 6–8 present the added experiments. The original ERF figure is relocated and renumbered from Figure 6 to Figure 9; downstream Figures 7–8 and architecture Table 5 are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional validation of SASF's portability and operator trade-offs, another detector-head evaluation, and clearer implementation and ERF details. These improve support and reproducibility around an unchanged central contribution. The gains are limited by the Vim adaptation changing pooling and state size alongside SASF, and by a new efficiency overstatement: Table 6 lists 740 GFLOPs for Spatial-Mamba-T versus 737 for NAT-T despite claiming fewer FLOPs. Overall, the additions offer an incremental net improvement.
